Q: How can I exclude the conditions evaluation report from the console of a Spring boot application? A:

Modern (2026) way is setting this property:

spring.test.print-condition-evaluation-report=false

Q: Elastic Beanstalk "You cannot migrate an environment to a VPC" error when updating ENV propert(no VPC changes) A: 
This is a known console bug in AWS Elastic Beanstalk that occurs when the console incorrectly detects VPC configuration changes even when you're not modifying any VPC settings.

**Why This Happens:**

The AWS console has an overly aggressive validation check for VPC migrations. When you edit any configuration section (environment properties, service access, etc.), the console reads the current VPC configuration and compares it against what it thinks should be there. Sometimes this comparison logic triggers a false positive, throwing the "cannot migrate to VPC" error even though no actual migration is being attempted.

**Solutions:**

**Option 1: Use the EB CLI (Recommended)**

The CLI bypasses the console's buggy validation logic:

```bash
# Set a single environment variable
eb setenv YOUR_VAR_NAME=value

# Set multiple variables
eb setenv VAR1=value1 VAR2=value2

# Or use AWS CLI
aws elasticbeanstalk update-environment \
  --environment-name your-env-name \
  --option-settings Namespace=aws:elasticbeanstalk:application:environment,OptionName=YOUR_VAR,Value=yourvalue

Option 2: Configuration Files

Add environment variables via .ebextensions:

# .ebextensions/env-vars.config
option_settings:
  aws:elasticbeanstalk:application:environment:
    YOUR_VAR_NAME: "your_value"

Then deploy:

eb deploy

Option 3: Clear Browser Cache

Sometimes stale session data causes this:

  1. Clear your browser cache and cookies for AWS console
  2. Log out and back in
  3. Try the configuration change again

Option 4: Use a Different Configuration Section

If you're trying to update environment properties, try using the "Software" configuration section instead of direct environment property updates. The different UI paths sometimes have different validation logic.

Why Your Setup Triggers This:

Since your environment was created about a year ago and you've only managed it through the console, it's likely that:

  • The console's internal state tracking has become inconsistent
  • A recent AWS platform update changed validation logic
  • Your environment's metadata needs refreshing

The EB CLI or configuration files are more reliable for ongoing management and won't have this issue.

Q: Objects.equals(null, null); should return false A:

I disagree with your assertion that a reference is not a value. A reference is a value that refers to a value ... or more specifically an object. (It cannot refer to a value of a non-reference type.) By extension, null is the distinguished reference value that doesn't refer to any object.

See https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-4.html#jls-4.1 which states:

There is also a special null type, the type of the expression null (§3.10.8, §15.8.1), which has no name.

Because the null type has no name, it is impossible to declare a variable of the null type or to cast to the null type.

The null reference is the only possible value of an expression of null type.

The null reference can always be assigned or cast to any reference type (§5.2, §5.3, §5.5).

In practice, the programmer can ignore the null type and just pretend that null is merely a special literal that can be of any reference type.
